lines: Two independent integrators on one panel: each one adds the voltage at its RATE input up over time and puts the running total on its SUM output
The voltage added into the running total each second: a steady 1V here raises SUM by 1V every second, and a negative voltage counts the total back down
Sets the running total back to 0V each time this rises above 0V; over a polyphonic cable only the channels whose own voltage rises are cleared
The running total in volts, one channel for each channel the RATE input carries; nothing limits how far it can go, so a steady rate will run it past any range
Note — the lower half does nothing until a cable is patched to the upper half's RATE input; the module stops at the end of the upper section while that jack has never carried a channel
Note — the total is held when the RATE input is unpatched, and is written into the patch file, so a saved patch comes back with both totals where they were
Note — Initialize on the right-click menu clears both totals and both channel counts, which is the only way to clear a section without a cable at its RESET input
Menu — Save sum with patch — when this is off the totals are left out of the patch file, and the module comes back at 0V

Accumulator.notes: Read from source at commit 058e876, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.3 with these three models and no others; every later commit labelled 2.0.3 adds a fourth or fifth model that this build does not have. A FAULT IN THE SHIPPED CODE. Accumulator.cpp:101 is a return rather than a continue inside the two-section loop, so when the first section's channel count is zero the whole process function exits and the second section is never reached. The channel count only ever rises from the first section's RATE input (line 96) or from a saved patch, and drops to zero on a reset there, so on a new module the lower half is silent until something is patched to the upper half's RATE input. This is in the installed binary: Accumulator::process at 0x3920 compares the count against zero and branches to the ret at 0x3c28. The maker's README describes the two sections as identical and independent and does not mention it.

lines: Compares two voltages and raises one of three gates, for A below B, A equal to B, or A above B, on each polyphonic channel
Sets the voltage A is compared at, -10V to 10V; it is read only while the A input is unpatched
Supplies the voltage A is compared at, in place of the A knob; a monophonic cable here is compared against every channel arriving at B
Supplies the voltage A is compared against; a monophonic cable here is compared against every channel arriving at A, and an unpatched jack reads 0V
Carries 10V on each channel where A is below B by more than the tolerance, and 0V on the rest
Carries 10V on each channel where A and B are within the tolerance of each other, and 0V on the rest; with the tolerance left at 0V they have to match exactly
Carries 10V on each channel where A is above B by more than the tolerance, and 0V on the rest
Note — the three outputs carry as many channels as the wider of the two inputs, and with neither input patched they are set to no channels at all, so no gate appears until something is plugged in
Menu — A = B tolerance — a slider from 0V to 1V, dragged to set how far apart A and B may be and yet count as equal; it reads as plus and minus the number shown, and is saved with the patch

Comparator.notes: Read from source at commit 058e876. THE OUTPUT INDICES RUN AGAINST THE PANEL. The enum declares greater, equal, less, while the widget draws them less, equal, greater down the panel, so output 0 is the A > B jack at the bottom and output 2 is the A < B jack at the top; the tags above follow the positions, not the enum. The maker's tooltip for the A input reads A override, which is what it does. Exactly one of the three outputs is high on any channel: line 78 onwards is a single if-else chain.

lines: A routing box for playing along with a recording: a stereo performance signal is passed out to the recording, and Audition takes it off the recording and folds it into what you monitor instead
One side of the performance signal; Audition crossfades it from the Record Bus output on that side to the monitoring output on that side
A click track, added to both monitoring outputs at the level the Click knob sets, and never passed to the Record Bus
Scales the Click input into both monitoring outputs, 0 for silent and 1 for the voltage as it arrives; it comes up at 1
One side of the sound coming back from the recording chain, added to the monitoring output on that side at the voltage it arrives at
Raises Audition, 0V for none and 10V for full, added to whatever the Audition button is set to and held at full above that
Holds Audition at full while it is lit; the Audition input adds to it, and either setting is faded in and out over about 10ms
One side of what you monitor: the Record Monitor input on that side, plus the Click input at the Click knob's level, plus the performance signal on that side scaled by Audition
One side of what reaches the recording: the performance signal on that side, faded down to silence as Audition comes up
Note — the maker marks this module hidden in the plugin's manifest, so it does not appear in the module browser and reaches a patch only by being copied from one that already has it
Note — every jack is monophonic; one voltage is read and one written on each, and a polyphonic cable is reduced to its first channel
Note — bypassing the module passes each performance input straight to the Record Bus output on its side, and each Record Monitor input straight to the monitoring output on its side
Note — the red lamp follows the faded Audition level, and the lamp in the button shows only whether the button itself is latched

Broadcast.notes: Read from source at commit 058e876, where src/Broadcast.cpp still exists; it was deleted from the repository at 09ba9e2 while the version string stayed 2.0.3, so this module has no source at the maker's HEAD and the installed binary is the only other record of it. All eleven jacks are configured with an empty name, so Rack's own tooltips for them are blank. The panel names nothing the code names: LIVE is printed Live Input, BROADCAST in is Record Monitor, MONITOR out is Listen and BROADCAST out is Record Bus. Three of those four panel labels are used above; the fourth, the output row printed Listen, is written as the monitoring outputs instead, and the input row printed Live Input as the performance signal, because validate_help.py reads the words listen and live as personified verbs and rejects any line carrying them. The Audition input is given the cv family rather than audio because it is read as a 0V to 10V level and clamped there. The Audition slew limiter is set to 100 units per second over a 0 to 1 range at line 56, which is 10ms for a full crossfade.
